input.rationale: Experiment for the sharpened investigation 0bfc2ea5a9e94316982943d306eefbf6-question-0. It reuses the harness file already in the draft, now extended with a hand-built three-node cluster made from the library's own in-memory transport, store and snapshot store so that one node's LogStore can be wrapped to return an allowed error from StoreLogs. The history staged is a legal single-cluster one: the initial leader is partitioned, keeps accepting client work into its own log (uncommitted), the remaining two voters elect a leader at a higher term and commit different entries at the same indices, then the partition heals. The control runs the identical history with a healthy store. Native local feedback on this harness in a scratch copy inside draft produced the expected divergence between the two cases, so the prediction is credible but is not treated as the conclusion; the retained execution decides. The earlier leadership-transfer harness was kept in the same file so the file remains self-contained and the first witness stays reproducible from it.

scope.description: Two subtests run the same legal history, differing only in whether the node's store fails the StoreLogs call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion. Each case builds three voters with NewInmemTransport, NewInmemStore (wrapped by a legal fault-injecting LogStore implementing the interface), NewInmemSnapshotStore and the package MockFSM, bootstrapped with the library's BootstrapCluster and started with NewRaft. The initial leader is then isolated at the transport level, keeps two Apply calls in its own log, the other two nodes elect a leader at a higher term and commit two entries, and the partition is healed. The case records: the diverging node's cached certificate (getLastEntry), its reported LastIndex, commit and applied indexes, the wrapped store's FirstIndex/LastIndex and whether GetLog of the certificate index errors, and the store's StoreLogs attempt/delivery counters, sampled every 25 ms for 1500 ms after the heal and once more 1200 ms after the fault (if any) is removed. The leader's own certificate and store counters are recorded alongside.
assumptions: A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, not corruption of an acknowledged durable write; the wrapper returns such an error without touching the underlying store.

The staged history is a legal single-cluster history: the diverging node's tail entries were appended while it was partitioned and therefore uncommitted, and the majority's replacement entries are committed at a higher term.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so nonprogress is produced by the library's logic rather than by transport faults.
The fault is armed only on the diverging node and only after the majority has committed its replacement entries, so the failing call is the StoreLogs that follows the conflicting-suffix deletion.
excluded: No production code is modified; the wrapper implements the public LogStore interface only.
No snapshot install, restart or leader-side compaction is performed, so the question of whether those repair the state stays open in this execution.

experiment.prefix: Each case prints CA_EVENT JSON lines: truncation_before_heal (the two nodes' probes before the partition heals), truncation_after_heal (probes plus the 1500 ms sampling arrays cert_index_samples, store_last_samples, store_attempts), and truncation_after_disarm (a probe 1200 ms after the fault is removed). Probes carry cert_last_index/cert_last_term, reported_last, commit_index, applied_index, store_first/store_last, store_attempts/store_delivered and cert_entry_error.

scope.description: Two cases in one execution, both driving the public API of the unmodified library in-process with the package's in-memory transport, stores and snapshot store. Case A (control): MakeCluster(3) with default protocol version 3, then LeadershipTransferToServer to a voter. Case B: MakeCluster(3) plus a separate MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1) merged and fully connected, then AddNonvoter for that node, wait until the non-voter has learned the 4-server configuration and caught up to a freshly committed proof entry, then LeadershipTransferToServer to that non-voter. Each case records the leader's configuration with suffrages, the future's error and duration, the target's and incumbent's state and term, timestamped state sampling for 500 ms, the observer stream of RequestVoteRequests (candidate id, term, log position, transfer flag), and whether the voters hold one leader again afterwards.
assumptions: In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so any nonprogress or state change observed is produced by the library's own logic rather than by a transport fault.
inmemConfig timeouts (heartbeat/election/lease 50 ms, commit 5 ms) make election and recovery observable inside a short window.
The non-voter's membership and catch-up are established through the library's own producers: AddNonvoter plus a committed proof entry the target has applied.
Protocol version 3 is the default, which is required for both AddNonvoter and LeadershipTransferToServer.
excluded: No production function is modified, wrapped or re-implemented; only the public API and the library's observer/testing facilities are used.
No artificial clock, timeout injection or fault injection is used.

basis.prefix: Each test prints CA_EVENT JSON lines. Control case: control_transfer_before / control_transfer_after. Non-voter case: nonvoter_transfer_before / nonvoter_transfer_after / nonvoter_transfer_recovery. RequestVoteRequest observations carry candidate_id, term, transfer_flagged; sampled_transitions carries t_ms, node, state, term.

result.summary: Submitted the wedge experiment: the harness now stages the legal partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history on a hand-built three-node cluster with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper, running the same history with and without an injected StoreLogs error and sampling the certificate, store contents and store-attempt counters for 1.5 s plus a post-disarm window.
